standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Definition \ref{algebra-definition-formally-smooth} and Definition \ref{definition-formally-smooth}, cited at proof lines 9186-9188 and 9194

standard_prerequisites.name: Continuity of a ring map for adic topologies is equivalent to a power of the source ideal mapping into the target ideal

standard_prerequisites.use: Translates the continuity of the structure maps and of the constructed lifts into statements about powers of ideals.

core_obligations: Assume algebraic formal smoothness and describe the topology on the target by an ideal (proof lines 9186-9190).
Use continuity of the structure map to get a lifting and check that the lift is continuous because a square of a power of the ideal dies (proof lines 9191-9200).
Show the converse implication for two adic topologies by the same argument (proof lines 9201-9206).
In the other direction, compute the powers of the two ideals that force continuity of the source map and then obtain the dotted arrow from the hypothesis (proof lines 9206-9210).
proof_roadmap: From algebraic formal smoothness to adic formal smoothness (proof lines 9186-9200).
Reduction of the second statement to (1) (proof lines 9201-9205).
Converse by computing powers of the ideals (proof lines 9206-9210).
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares formal smoothness in the sense of the earlier algebraic definition with formal smoothness for adic topologies: the former implies the latter for any linear topology on the source and any pre-adic topology on the target making the map continuous, and for two adic topologies the condition can be checked with the discrete topology on the source. Both directions are continuity bookkeeping around the lifting property: a solid diagram with continuous structure map is turned into a lifting problem for the algebraic notion, and the resulting lift is shown to be continuous by computing that a suitable power of the adic ideal maps into the square-zero kernel, with the converse handled by the symmetric computation of powers of the two ideals.
